column1: # comment: "Imagination slice alignments \u2014 the as-if attitude flavour of mind and the content-origin / reality-monitoring value vocabulary. EXTERNAL FRAMEWORKS NAMED IN PROSE (no stable, resolvable RDF namespace available): * Source-monitoring framework (Marcia K. Johnson): the cognitive account of how an agent attributes the SOURCE of a memory or thought \u2014 perceived vs imagined vs told \u2014 is the direct basis of the gmeow:ContentOrigin value vocabulary (gmeow:originPerceived / originRemembered / originImagined / \u2026). It is published as psychology literature, not as an OWL-resolvable ontology, so no TermEquivalence row can be written; the conceptual debt is recorded here. * Mimesis as make-believe (Kendall Walton): the philosophy-of-fiction account of imagining as a prop-governed game of make-believe underpins gmeow:imagines and the fiction = licensed-imagining bridge to gmeow:veridicalityLicensedFalsehood (deception slice). No stable IRI vocabulary exists; named in prose only. * Reality-monitoring (Johnson & Raye): the perceived-vs-imagined discrimination that gmeow:contentOrigin operationalises for agent memory \u2014 the recalled-vs-confabulated test. No resolvable namespace; prose only. The gmeow:imagines / gmeow:supposes attitudes and the gmeow:imaginedWorld link have no stable external IRI counterpart (possible-world semantics is realised internally by the logic slice's logic:World, a gmeow: term, not an external vocabulary) and are intentionally left unmapped."
# # No frame-selecting mapping (Principle 9): GMEOW does not assert a single 'correct' theory of imagination or source-monitoring; the value-vocab members are co-equal.

column6: gmeow:originGenerated marks content whose source is a generative process (machine synthesis); prov:Generation is the activity by which an entity comes into being. The shared notion is generative origin, but PROV is activity-provenance and gmeow:originGenerated is a reality-monitoring content-origin value — loose relatedMatch only.
